notes_markdown:
**Tethered shooting, per-photo edit history with undo, look profiles,
a RAW denoiser, windowed big-library scans, and a top-to-bottom visual
refresh** — everything that has landed while release publishing was
paused.

### Tethered shooting (Sony first)

- **Plug in a camera and shoot.** With a Sony body in PC Remote mode
  (validated live on an a7C II), every shot appears in culler moments
  after the shutter: the JPEG shows the instant it lands and the RAW
  attaches behind it, so the screen never waits on a 47 MB file, and
  bursts drain at full wire speed. Downloads retry on their own and
  the app stays awake for the whole session. Any other camera gets the
  same tethered ingest; remote control is Sony-only for now, and
  culler says so honestly.
- **Remote shutter**: `Shift+Space` fires the camera from culler —
  from the grid too.
- **Live view** (`B`): the camera's live feed takes the photo's place
  on the cull screen (about 25 fps over USB). A fresh capture holds
  briefly for review, and `Shift+Space` fires straight through it.
- **Hold focus** (`L`): park the half-press once and every following
  shot fires instantly at that focus — for catching the exact moment.
- **Timer**: intervalometer, self-timer and bulb exposures from one
  rail button, with a live countdown in the corner readout.
- **Camera control from the info panel**: aperture, shutter speed, ISO
  (with Auto), exposure compensation and white balance as − / +
  steppers, plus manual-focus nudge keys `[` / `]` (Shift for coarse,
  Cmd for fine). Rapid steps queue smoothly — no waiting between
  clicks.
- **Camera vitals**: battery, drive mode and shots remaining in the
  corner readout and the info panel — polled gently, always yielding
  to photo transfer.
- **Session folders in the sources pane.** Tethered shots land in a
  dated folder per day, and the camera row expands into past sessions:
  continue one, rename, delete (two-click confirm) or start a fresh
  one — browsable even with no camera plugged in.
- **Live mirror**: every shot can back up automatically as it lands,
  to a folder or straight to an Immich server, with retries and a loud
  warning if the destination goes away — a dead destination never
  holds up newer shots.
- **USB link speed** in the info panel ("USB 2.0 · 480 Mb/s"), with a
  nudge when a faster port would help — a slow hub is the usual reason
  transfers crawl.

### Develop

- **Edit history and snapshots, per photo.** `⌘Z` / `⌘⇧Z` undo and
  redo everything — ratings, flags, develop, crop. A History card in
  the develop panel lists every step: click one to restore that state
  (non-destructively — the restore is itself undoable), or promote it
  to a named snapshot; a Snapshots card keeps named states to return
  to. All of it persists in the sidecar and survives restarts.
- **Look profiles replace the Match JPEG button.** The develop panel's
  look picker applies a complete camera-style look — tone, color and
  per-hue adjustments — with the exposure matched per shot. Built-in:
  Vivid (Sony); drop your own profiles in `~/.culler/looks/`. The
  picture style the camera recorded in the photo is recognized and
  pre-highlighted (never applied on its own), and **Auto (`Shift+A`)
  on a RAW applies it** — one key per photo gives a whole set the
  camera's own look.
- **Color Mix**: eight per-hue bands of hue / saturation / luminance —
  as sliders or a draggable curve — for the color work a global
  saturation slider can't do. Saved to the sidecar like everything
  else.
- **RAW noise reduction.** Developing a RAW now applies denoising —
  ISO-aware on Auto, adjustable via the new Denoise slider
  (double-click returns to Auto). Dark, high-ISO shots stop looking
  grainier than the camera's JPEG, and exports carry it too.
- **A redesigned develop panel**: grouped cards, rebuilt sliders with
  finer damped drags, scroll-to-nudge (the panel no longer scrolls
  underneath), click-the-value-to-type, double-click-to-reset, and
  values that light up when off default.
- **White-balance eyedropper.** "Pick gray point" in the Color card
  (or press `Q`): click something neutral in the photo (a gray card
  works great) and
  Temp/Tint are set so it renders neutral — real Kelvin on a RAW,
  slider offsets on a JPEG. Clipped spots are refused with a clear
  message, and `Esc` cancels.
- **Match Look no longer fits automatically.** Entering `M` freezes
  the set and changes nothing; the fit runs when you press the new
  **Match** button in the panel, and **Reset all** returns every photo
  to how it was at entry — so a fit you don't like is one click to
  inspect and one click to back out.
- **Match a scattered series.** Select photos from anywhere in the
  library, `Shift+Y` to show just the selection, `M` — Match Look now
  works over exactly that set (a progression series, not just a
  burst), with an honest count when a selection exceeds the 24-photo
  window.
- **Matched crops.** `C` now works inside Match Look: crop the
  reference to set the series' frame, then each other photo opens in
  an **align view** — the reference stays put, solid, while your photo
  rides on top as a faint overlay that you drag, scroll-to-size and
  straighten until the subjects line up. `\` previews the result
  solid. Reset means "back to the reference's placement", and — like
  the rest of the session — nothing is written until `M` commits.
- **Re-rendering from inside a stack updates the cover on exit.**
  `G` into a stack, develop, `J`, `G` out used to keep showing the old
  version until you switched albums — the collapsed cover now swaps to
  the fresh upload immediately.
- **Crops show on already-uploaded edits immediately.** A new crop on
  a photo whose display is culler's own uploaded render used to stay
  invisible everywhere until the next `J` — committing a matched
  series then looked like nothing happened. It now shows at once in
  every view (scrolling, grid, previews), and `J` bakes it into the
  server copy as before.
- **The crop controls are a side pane now.** They used to float over
  the top of the photo — and over the landmark panes — as a card;
  cropping now docks its controls on the right like the develop panel,
  so nothing ever covers the image while you frame it.
- **Landmark align.** When poses shift too much for hand-dragging,
  align by matching points instead: `Shift+C` (or the **Landmarks**
  chip) in the align view opens a three-pane layout — the reference,
  your photo, and the live result. Click 2–8 distinctive points on the
  reference (an ankle, the nose, a hip ridge), click the same numbered
  points on your photo, and from the second point the crop solves
  itself — position, size and tilt at once. `Tab` skips a point that's
  out of view (any two shared points are enough), a magnifier follows
  the cursor for precision, `⌫` undoes, right-click (or the hover `×`)
  removes a specific point, and `Enter` accepts and moves to the next
  photo. Nothing is written until `M` commits, as ever.
- **Landmark-view captions sit under their photos.** Each pane's
  caption used to anchor to the bottom of the screen, where it collided
  with the status line into overlapping text; captions now ride
  directly beneath the photo they describe.
- **Match Look sessions now write history.** Committing with `M`
  records one entry per changed photo ("Match look" / "Matched crop"),
  so `Cmd/Ctrl+Z` can step a committed session back per photo.
- **Matched preview.** `K` inside Match Look shows the whole set as a
  grid with its live tone and crop — the series exactly as it will
  commit, tracking every slider move; click a photo to focus it.
- **The eyedropper works inside Match Look.** `Q` on the focused photo
  neutralizes its white balance — the per-photo color step a
  months-apart series needs before the tone fit. Samples stay with the
  session: `M` commits them, `Esc` unwinds them.
- **The crop window slides past the frame.** When a tighter-framed
  photo needs its subject placed beyond its own edge — matching a
  series often does — keep dragging: the outside renders and exports as
  clean white padding, in the editor, the preview and the file alike.
- **The align view has a legend.** A caption under the photo names
  which is which (`solid: <reference> · faint: <this photo>`), both
  while aligning and in the result preview.
- **Full controls in the align view.** Corner handles on the frame
  drag-scale your photo, `↑`/`↓` size it from the keyboard,
  `Cmd/Ctrl+arrows` nudge its position (`Shift` = coarser steps
  everywhere), and a quiet outline shows where your photo's actual
  edges are.
- **Fixed: the double apply after saving a JPEG-only photo.** On a
  photo without a RAW file, `J`'s render replaced the display and the
  crop, rotation and tone were then applied *again* on top — a tighter,
  re-rotated picture on screen, and a second `J` made it worse. Baked
  renders now paint plain everywhere (main view, filmstrip, grids,
  Compare), and a re-`J` re-uploads the same picture.

### Immich

- **Your edits and history now live on the server.** On a remote
  photo, `J` saves the develop settings, crop, full edit history and
  snapshots with the photo on the server, alongside the rendered JPEG
  it already uploads — reload the library or open it from another
  machine and everything is back where you left it. Edits you haven't
  committed with `J` stay local to the session.
- **Big libraries open in windows.** Past roughly 5,000 photos, a
  library no longer loads whole: the newest couple of thousand open
  immediately and older months load as you approach them. Markers show
  where the gaps are (click one to load it), `Shift+S` opens a date
  picker that jumps straight to any month, and the sources row offers
  "Load all" with a live tally.
- **Scans recover instead of failing.** Failed pages retry with
  backoff on their own, the partial-scan warning gained a one-click
  **Retry**, and scanning is gentler on modest home servers.
- **Both current Immich generations are supported.** culler discovers
  the server's API version and reports a compatibility verdict when
  you add or open a server. On v3 servers, archived photos stay out of
  the timeline and culler's edits keep their identity.
- **The info panel** (`I`): camera, lens, file size, place and
  description for every photo on every source. On Immich it grows
  server powers: edit the description in place, Favorite (the same
  axis as your Pick — starring works both ways), the people the server
  recognized, and the photo's albums.
- **Album picker** (`Shift+I`): sort photos into server albums without
  leaving the cull — type to filter, Space toggles membership.
- **Locked folder** (v3 servers): move a photo into the server's
  locked folder from the info panel. It's one-way from culler — only
  Immich's own web app can bring it back, and the panel says so.
- **Favorites and flags on unrated photos now stick.** Newer servers
  reject the "no stars" value culler used to send, so every favorite
  or flag write on an unrated photo failed and silently retried
  forever. culler now says "no rating" the way the server expects.
- **No more black previews after `J`.** The uploaded render becomes
  the photo's preview immediately instead of racing the server's
  thumbnail job, and a preview that failed to download retries when
  you return to the photo.
- **Re-rendering an edit is safe.** `J` on an already-edited photo
  renders from the RAW again (never from its own previous output) and
  keeps filenames sane instead of stacking "-edit" onto "-edit" — and
  when nothing actually changed, it recognizes the identical render
  and leaves the stack alone (that corner case used to trash the
  stack's own cover, hiding the whole stack from the server's
  timeline).
- **Same-named photos say where they live**: photos with the same
  filename in different folders carry a quiet folder tag in the
  overlay, so stacking no longer looks broken.

### Uploads

- **Already-stored photos skip in milliseconds.** Before any bytes
  move, a checksum precheck asks the server what it already has —
  re-running a batch flies through everything that made it the first
  time.
- **Retry is the button.** After a batch with errors the primary
  button becomes "Retry N failed…": one click re-runs the batch, the
  precheck skips the stored photos, and the summary names which photos
  failed and why.
- **Honest progress**: the batch's total size up front, a
  byte-accurate bar per file, "838 MB left · 3.1 MB/s", a live speed
  graph, and an amber note when nothing has moved for a while.
- **Big files on slow connections no longer fail at exactly
  20 seconds** — a whole-request time limit was cutting them off;
  uploads now take the time they need.
- **Move to Immich, safely.** When a batch is verified fully stored on
  the server, a "Trash N originals…" offer appears under the summary:
  arm with one click, confirm with a second — and at that moment the
  server re-verifies every single file once more. Anything it can't
  vouch for is kept, and if the server can't be reached, nothing is
  touched. Originals go to the system Trash.
- **Sending files to the Trash is instant** — it used to route through
  Finder, which on some Macs sat out a two-minute timeout and failed.

### Export

- **Exports now match straight-out-of-camera quality**: JPEGs encode
  at quality 95 with full-resolution color by default (a saved setting
  keeps its old value).
- **The JPEG Quality slider is always reachable**: it now has its own
  card in the batch panel on every source — it also governs `J`, which
  quietly followed it all along; the first `J` mentions it once.

### Multi-select

- **Select several photos and act on them at once.** `Cmd/Ctrl`+click
  toggles a photo in the filmstrip or Grid, `Shift`+click selects the
  run, and from the keyboard `Y` toggles the current photo,
  `Shift`+arrows sweep, `Cmd/Ctrl+A` selects the whole view and
  `Cmd/Ctrl+D` clears. Selected photos wear a blue check chip, the
  corner readout and Grid header count the set, the marking keys
  (pick/reject/stars/labels) act on all of it when you're on a
  selected photo, and the batch panel's Scope menu gains
  **Selected (N)** so any batch action runs on exactly those.
- **`Shift+Y` shows only the selected photos** — cull a hand-picked
  shortlist with every tool, the grid included. The view tracks the
  selection live (deselecting drops the photo on the spot), and
  clearing the selection returns to All with a note.
- **Sweeping deselection**: deselect a photo, and the very next
  `Shift`+click or `Shift`+arrows deselects the whole run — pruning a
  big selection is one gesture. `Shift`+click ranges always start at
  the photo you're on.

### The new look

- **A top-to-bottom visual refresh.** Every panel — batch, crop
  toolbar, sources form, timer, help — now shares one consistent dark
  design: uniform control sizes, type, forms and keycap chips. The
  help overlay is grouped by topic and finally scrolls instead of
  clipping, and the phantom resize cursor on the side rails is gone.

### Fixes

- The info panel's **Move to locked folder** action now looks like a
  button (hover highlight) instead of a bare text line.
- Grid view: `Shift+Space` now fires the tethered shutter as the menu
  says (it used to peek the photo instead).
- `Shift+A` auto tone on a RAW now reads the RAW histogram, matching
  what the panel's Auto button always did.
- Filenames arriving from a server or camera are reduced to a safe
  name before writing, so a malicious or confused source can no longer
  write outside the chosen folder.
- `Shift+J` (overwrite JPEG) now verifies its backup and writes it
  atomically — a stale or partial backup can no longer cost a camera
  original.
- A sidecar that exists but can't be read is left untouched instead of
  templated over — other tools' metadata in it survives.
- A batch finishing while Compare, Survey or Match Look was open could
  crash or mark the wrong photo; it now waits until you leave the
  view.
- Re-adding a server you already saved updates its API key instead of
  creating a duplicate entry — the natural key-rotation path.
- Grid view: clicking a photo far from the current one no longer makes
  the surrounding thumbnails flicker while they re-render.
- Re-editing an already-uploaded edit (a new crop or grade, then `J`)
  no longer silently re-uploads the previous picture when the RAW
  can't be downloaded or decoded — the upload stops and the status
  line names the real cause, so the retry actually carries your edit.
- Downloading a large RAW (for `J`'s re-render or 1:1 zoom) now gets
  the same generous time budget as uploads instead of dying at 20
  seconds on a slow connection.
- Match Look's align view: the size handles now sit on *your photo's*
  outline corners instead of the reference frame — the reference
  carries no drag controls.
